The broader quiz-authoring purpose may be consequential, but this particular pattern appears peripheral and conventional.

The evidence does not explicitly establish that every note receives exactly the same uneditable relation vocabulary, and relation menus for ideation are useful but no longer especially novel.

ratings.reason: The quote clearly shows one named AI action bound to an existing topic group, with generated questions returned and linked to that group. That is a legible atomic action, but the evidence shows only one button—not a small system-wide menu whose complete action set appears on every unit. Question generation for reflection is useful and portable, though fairly established.

This is the cleanest structural match: topics and subtopics are the units, and each is supported by the same four named prompts—Explanation, Example, Exercise, and Exercise Solution. The units × actions structure is explicit and highly transferable. However, selecting canned pedagogical operations is an obvious and now-settled design move; the supplied evidence does not establish outcome improvements sufficient for a higher impact score.

The enumerated Actions and Actors strongly suggest a fixed Cartesian interaction space in which a prepared move is applied to a selected target. The tangible, investigative framing is a comparatively interesting embodiment and could meaningfully structure fact-checking practice. Still, the quote does not explicitly say that every target exposes every action or that each pairing initiates AI generation, while several actors are roles or evidence sources rather than conventional content units.

The template supplies three fixed, named reflection questions, and clicking one generates an answer about the relevant competitor or column. Both sides of the interaction are concrete enough to rebuild, and the pattern transfers to many unit-based repositories. The evidence does not quite prove universal availability across every unit, and canned reflection questions are a competent refinement rather than a major reframing of the design space.

Sensecape visibly binds a named generation action to a selected node: choose the node, invoke Questions, and receive generated questions. Node-based expansion is portable and useful for sensemaking. But the supplied quote demonstrates only one button and cannot establish a fixed, complete menu repeated across all nodes; the broader system may be influential, but that cannot be credited to this pattern from the available evidence.

A named Generate Summary command is compatible with an atomic AI action, but the quote does not identify its target unit, show a menu of multiple actions, or establish repetition across units. Summarization buttons are highly conventional, and neither their distinctive effect nor their centrality to GLITTER can be judged from this evidence.

Tangible prompt cubes plausibly encode prepared actions that pupils apply to their texts, making this an interesting physical interpretation of constrained AI input. The quote, however, supplies no action names, menu size, evidence that all cubes apply to every text unit, or generation response. Its tangible and child-learning dependencies also make direct transplantation less straightforward than a software menu.

The quote identifies five apparently fixed information aids associated with each of four paraphrased suggestions, giving meaningful evidence of a repeated units × options structure. These aids could improve users' ability to assess paraphrases and transfer to other candidate-selection interfaces. However, the evidence calls them aids rather than invocable actions and does not show that selecting each one runs a generation call, so the match to the pattern's defining interaction is incomplete and the move is fairly derivative.
